newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Rising Dhaka stocks may scare off overseas funds.
newsitem.headline: Rising Dhaka stocks may scare off overseas funds.

text.p: Bangladesh's stock market has surged to a record high amid euphoria over the government's privatisation plans, but analysts fear the rise may discourage overseas funds.

The Dhaka Stock Exchange benchmark index jumped 37.66 points or 2.22 percent to 1,726.53 on Wednesday. The surge was prompted by news that the government would soon offload shares of 15 public companies, brokers said.
Market capitalisation rose to $2.84 billion on Wednesday from $2.0 billion on August 1. It was only $452 million at the end of 1994.
Share prices also rose sharply on Thursday, with heavy gains in some engineering scrips.

"Foreign institutions have been very hesitant to come into the market at the (current) valuations, prefering to take profits and wait on the sidelines for more reasonably-priced IPO (intitial public offering) stocks," Brenda Trenowden, head of research with Peregrine Capital, said on Thursday.
She said the DSE index had surged because of new funds from local retail investors chasing too few stocks.
Broker Abdul Rashid said some local investors were holding huge blocks of shares. "They don't want to sell, creating a shortfall and sending the prices up."
Trenowden said: "We believe that the market is fundamentally overvalued, but that the retail demand has yet to be satisfied."

She said the bullish trend, which was fuelled initially by overwhelming interest in Chittagong Cement and Singer Bangladesh, had now spread to the broad index including laggards in pharmaceuticals, textiles, food, footware and leather.

"The market is expected to remain firm and buoyant. The prices may further rise as too many investors aim at fewer prospective shares. The highly priced scrips will continue to gain as there is short supply of stocks," said broker Khurshid Alam.
Brokers said Wednesday's jump in the market was primarily due to the news that the government would soon sell off shares in 15 public companies.
The government on Tuesday said it also planned to privatise 41 state-owned companies by July 1997.
"Retailers returned with big expectations after the news. They bought almost recklessly," one broker said.

Rashid said the shortage of shares available for trading on the Chittagong Stock Exchange, the country's second bourse, might be another reason for rush of new investors in the Dhaka market and the consequent price rise.
Trenowden said the DSE index might continue to rise for another month.
"By year-end, we believe that there will be some correction and consolidation which will be a signal for foreign investors to come back into the market," she said.
